name: Tuckerman Ravine Trail
quote: climbs steadily to Hermit Lake Shelters (2.4 miles, 1800 feet elevation gain)
why: Climb from Pinkham Notch to the Hermit Lake Shelters below Tuckerman Ravine on Mt. Washington; 2.4 mi one-way doubled. The page gives no distance to the summit, so this covers only the Hermit Lake section.

name: Welch-Dickey Loop Trail
quote: continuing over the summits of both Welch and Dickey mountains over 4.4 miles
why: Loop over the open ledges of Welch and Dickey mountains near Waterville Valley.

name: Piper Trail
quote: The Piper Trail is a challenging trail that summits Mt. Chocorua (3,500 ft.) in 4.3 miles and 2,700 ft. of elevation gain.
why: Challenging out-and-back to the bare summit of Mt. Chocorua; 4.3 mi one-way doubled.

name: Carter Ledge Trail
quote: the Carter Ledge Trail is a strenuous 4.5 mile hike to the summit of Mt. Chocorua
why: Strenuous route from White Ledge Campground to the summit of Mt. Chocorua; 4.5 mi to the summit, doubled.

name: Mt. Osceola (Osceola Trailhead)
quote: The trail reaches the summit of Mt. Osceola in 3.2 miles with excellent views.
why: Out-and-back from Tripoli Road to the 4,000-footer Mt. Osceola; 3.2 mi one-way doubled.

name: Baldface Circle Trail
quote: the Baldface Circle Trail, which provides a 9 mile loop over North and South Baldface summits
why: Long loop over the open North and South Baldface summits, passing Emerald Pool.

name: Webster - Jackson Trail
quote: can be hiked as a 6.5 mile loop using the Webster Cliff Trail to connect the two summits
why: Crawford Notch loop over Mt. Webster and Mt. Jackson.

name: Signal Ridge Trail (Mt. Carrigain)
quote: It is a 5 mile hike up the Signal Ridge Trail to the tower
why: Climb to the observation tower on Mt. Carrigain; 5 mi up, doubled.

name: Mousilauke Carriage Road
quote: The historic Mousilauke Carriage Road ascends to the summit Mt. Moosilauke in 5.1 miles.
why: Historic carriage road to the alpine summit of Mt. Moosilauke; 5.1 mi one-way doubled. The page spells it 'Mousilauke'.

name: White Ledge Loop
quote: White Ledge Loop is a 4.4 mile loop trail to White Ledge (2,010 ft.); a 1,450 feet elevation gain.
why: Loop to the White Ledge viewpoint near Conway. The White Ledge Campground page calls it 'a moderate 4 mile loop'.

name: Mt. Tremont (Mt. Tremont Trailhead)
quote: The summit of Mt. Tremont (3,371 ft.) is reached in 2.8 miles, gaining 2,551 feet of elevation.
why: Steep climb from US 302 to the summit of Mt. Tremont; 2.8 mi one-way doubled.

name: Mount Kearsage (Kearsarge North Trailhead)
quote: Mount Kearsage (3,268ft.) can be summited using this approach in 3.1 miles and 2600 ft. of elevation gain.
why: Climb to the fire tower summit of Kearsarge North; 3.1 mi one-way doubled. 'Kearsage' is the page's spelling.

name: Three Ponds loop (Three Ponds Trailhead)
quote: an easy to moderate 5.3 mile loop back to the trailhead is possible via Donkey Hill Cut-off and the Kineo Trail
why: Easy-to-moderate loop past the Three Ponds shelter. The shorter option is 'an easy 2.2 mile walk' to the middle pond, one-way.

name: Hale Brook trail
quote: The trail ascends 2.2 miles to the summit of Mt. Hale and a connection with the Lend-A-Hand trail.
why: Short climb from Zealand Road to the summit of Mt. Hale; 2.2 mi one-way doubled.

name: Mt. Tecumseh (Mt Tecumseh Trailhead)
quote: The trail ascends Mt. Tecumseh, with good limited views from the summit at 2.5 mils.
why: Climb from Waterville Valley to the 4,000-footer Mt. Tecumseh; 2.5 mi to the summit, doubled. 'mils' [sic].

name: Wentworth Trail (Mt. Israel)
quote: reaches the summit of Mt. Israel (2,630 ft.) in 2.1 miles and 1,700 ft of elevation gain.
why: Climb from the Mead Base Conservation Center to the summit of Mt. Israel; 2.1 mi one-way doubled.

name: Moat Mountain (South Moat Mountain Trailhead)
quote: South Moat Mountain (2,770 ft.) can be reached in 2.7 miles from this trailhead
why: Climb near Conway to the open summit of South Moat Mountain; 2.7 mi one-way doubled. The quote is from the Saco district listing summary.

name: Snow's Mountain loop
quote: The trailhead accesses a 3.9 mile loop over Snow's Mountain with limited fine views.
why: Loop over Snow's Mountain in Waterville Valley.

name: Stinson Mountain Trail
quote: The Stinson Mountain Trail leaves from here and ascends 1.8 miles to Stinson Mt.
why: Short climb near Rumney to the summit of Stinson Mountain; 1.8 mi one-way doubled.

name: Black Mountain (Chippewa Trailhead)
quote: ascends the rocky summit of Black Mountain in 1.8 miles
why: Short climb to the rocky summit of Black Mountain; 1.8 mi one-way doubled. The quote is from the hiking listing summary.

name: Iron Mountain (Iron Mtn Trailhead)
quote: accesses Iron Mountain summit (2,726 ft.) in just 0.9 miles and 800 feet of elevation gain
why: Short, steep climb near Jackson to the Iron Mountain summit; 0.9 mi one-way doubled. The south cliffs are 0.7 mi farther.

name: Discovery Trail
quote: This 1.4 mile loop trail offers a living classroom in forest ecology.
why: Interpretive forest-ecology loop off the Kancamagus Highway.

name: Albany Brook Trail
quote: Albany Brook trail is an easy one mile trail
why: Easy walk along Crocker Pond to the north end of Round Pond (Evans Notch area).

name: Albany Mountain
quote: follow the Albany Mountain trail 1.5miles to the junction with the trail to the summit. Follow the summit spur for an additional 0.4 miles
why: Summit hike to open ledges of Albany Mountain; 1.5 mi trail + 0.4 mi spur, doubled.

name: Algonquin Trail
quote: ascends the southwest ridge of Sandwich Dome gaining its summit at 3,950 ft. in 4.5 miles
why: Climb of Sandwich Dome through the Sandwich Range Wilderness.

name: Big Attitash Mountain (Attitash Trailhead)
quote: Hikers reach Table Mountain (2,610 ft.) in 1.9 miles, Big Attitash Mountain (2,910 ft.) in 4.7 miles
why: Attitash Trail over Table Mountain to Big Attitash Mountain near Bartlett.

name: Basin Cascade Trail
quote: about 0.2 miles from the parking areas. The trail ascends along the very scenic Cascade Brook to its intersection with the Cascade Brook Trail, a segment of the Appalachian Trail, at 1.0 mile.
why: Cascades walk from The Basin in Franconia Notch; 0.2 + 1.0 mi, doubled.

name: Blueberry Mountain (Blueberry Mt S Trailhead)
quote: climbs to a short spur path to the summit at 2.8 miles
why: Blueberry Mountain Trail to the summit spur from the south trailhead (Benton).

name: Caps Ridge Trail
quote: The Caps Ridge trail accesses the summit of Mt. Jefferson and intersects with the Mt. Jefferson Loop trail at 2.6 miles.
why: Steep ridge route up Mt. Jefferson from Jefferson Notch, the highest trailhead in the Whites.

name: Middle Sister (Carter Ledge Trailhead)
quote: reaches the summit via Middle Sister Trail at 3.6 miles with 2000 feet of elevation gain
why: Climb to Middle Sister on the Chocorua massif from White Ledge Campground.

name: Church Pond
quote: Hikers can access Church Pond and the magnificent views it affords at 1.1 miles heading clockwise on this trail.
why: Pond walk off the Kancamagus Highway after fording the Swift River.

name: Bridal Veil Falls (Coppermine Trail)
quote: This easy to moderate trail parallels Coppermine Brook to reach Coppermine Shelter and beautiful Bridal Veil Falls at 2.5 miles.
why: Coppermine Trail along the brook to Bridal Veil Falls near Franconia.

name: Crawford Path
quote: This 8.5 mile spectacularly scenic trail is the oldest, continuously maintained, hiking path in America.
why: Historic path from Rte 302 over the southern Presidentials to Mt. Washington.

name: Daniel Webster Trail
quote: A direct 4.1 mile climb to the Presidential Range Alpine Zone and the Summit of Mount Madison.
why: Climb of Mt. Madison from Dolly Copp Campground.

name: Mt. Crawford (Davis Path)
quote: Daytrippers access Mt. Crawford at 2.2 miles from the parking lot.
why: Day hike on the Davis Path to Mt. Crawford in Crawford Notch.

name: Diana's Baths
quote: about a three quarter mile walk on the Moat Mountain Trail (northern terminus)
why: Accessible walk to pools and cascades on Lucy Brook near North Conway.

name: Doublehead Ski Trail
quote: The Doublehead Ski Trail reaches the cabin at 1.8 miles via a steep grade
why: Steep hike to the CCC cabin on North Doublehead summit in Jackson.

name: Drakes Brook Trail
quote: The Drakes Brook trail passes a spur to Fletcher's Cascades and then ascends to intersect with the Sandwich Mountain trail at 3.2 miles.
why: Trail past Fletcher's Cascades into the Sandwich Range Wilderness from Waterville Valley.

name: Sandwich Mountain Trail
quote: From the parking area Sandwich Mountain trail reaches the summit after 3.9 miles
why: Summit hike to Sandwich Dome from Rte 49 near Waterville Valley.

name: East Pond (Tripoli Rd)
quote: Reaching East Pond in 1.4 miles
why: Short hike to East Pond with a side loop to Little East Pond off Tripoli Road.

name: Edmands Path
quote: The 2.9 mile long Edmands Path affords the quickest route to the Mt. Eisenhower Loop
why: Graded path up to the Mt. Eisenhower Loop from Mt. Clinton Road.

name: Ethan Pond (Ethan Pond - Ripley Falls Trailhead)
quote: a gradual climb to AMC Ethan Pond Shelter (fee site) at 2.6 miles
why: Appalachian Trail climb from Crawford Notch to Ethan Pond.

name: Flat Mountain Pond Trail
quote: The Flat Mountain Pond Trail is 10.3 miles in length.
why: Long trail through the Sandwich Range Wilderness past Flat Mountain Pond between two trailheads.

name: Gale River Trail
quote: This 4 mile trail parallels Gale River before climbing steeply to access the Garfield Ridge trail
why: Most direct route to Galehead Hut, from Gale River Road.

name: Garfield Trail
quote: This trail accesses Garfield Ridge trail after 4.8 miles
why: Climb toward Mt. Garfield from Gale River Road.

name: Glencliff Trail
quote: the Glencliff Trail gains the bald popular summit of Mt. Moosilauke in 3.9 miles
why: Appalachian Trail route up Mt. Moosilauke from Glencliff.

name: Greeley Ponds (Kancamagus Hwy)
quote: This trailhead accesses the popular Greeley Ponds scenic area in 1.7 miles
why: Easy hike to the Greeley Ponds scenic area off the Kancamagus Highway.

name: Guinea Pond Trail
quote: From the gated Guinea Pond Trail the pond and the Wilderness area boundary can be reached within 2.0 miles.
why: Walk to Guinea Pond at the Sandwich Range Wilderness boundary.

name: Hammond Trail (Bald Mountain)
quote: The Hammond Trail acsends Bald Mountain (2,140 ft.) just below Mt. Chocorua, in 1.9 miles
why: Climb of Bald Mountain below Mt. Chocorua from Rte 16.

name: Horseshoe Pond Trail
quote: this trail is 1.1 miles over easy grades and connects to the Conant Trail
why: Easy pond trail off Deer Hill Rd. in the Evans Notch area.

name: Hubbard Brook Trail
quote: ends at a gate just off NH Rte.118 in Warren at 2.4 miles
why: Little-used trail past a beaver pond area near Warren.

name: Hutmen's Trail
quote: The trail is 3.1 miles in length, relatively flat and ends on Carter Notch Road.
why: Flat trail ending on Carter Notch Road near Jackson.

name: Jericho Road Trail
quote: The trail is a pleasant country road walk 3.2 miles to the site of the old Cooley Hill fire tower
why: Old road walk to the former Cooley Hill fire tower site near Easton.

name: Weeks Brook Trail
quote: The Weeks Brook Trail is 5.1 mile to the summit from South Chatham Road
why: Less-used route up Kearsarge North past Shingle Pond.

name: Livermore Trail
quote: This trail is 7.7 miles in length and accesses the Mt. Tripyramid Trail.
why: Old logging road through Waterville Valley between two trailheads.

name: Mad River Trail
quote: This moderate trail closely parallels the Mad River for 0.9 miles
why: Riverside trail to Waterville Valley Town Square.

name: Mountain Pond Loop
quote: This loop is 2.7 miles in total.
why: Loop around Mountain Pond with a shelter, off Slippery Brook Road.

name: Mt. Langdon Trail
quote: continues to the summit of Mount Parker (1,894 ft.), ending at the Mount Langdon Shelter in 2.9 miles
why: Trail from Bartlett over Mount Parker spur to the Mt. Langdon Shelter.

name: Mt. Stanton Trail
quote: several other small summits, and the Mt. Langdon Shelter at 5.4 miles
why: Ridge walk over Mt. Stanton and Mt. Langdon near Bartlett.

name: Nancy Cascade (Nancy Pond Trail)
quote: Nancy Cascade can be reached via Nancy Pond Trail at 2.4 miles.
why: Waterfall hike on Nancy Pond Trail off Rte 302.

name: North Twin Trail
quote: climbing steeply to intersect at the summit of North Twin with North Twin spur at 4.3 miles
why: Climb of North Twin along the Little River from Haystack Road.

name: Old Waterville Road Trail
quote: meeting a junction with the Yellowjacket and Pine Flats trails in 1.8 miles
why: Quiet access trail into the Smarts Brook area.

name: Owls Head Trail
quote: After 2.2 miles the Owls Head trail accesses fine limited views from the summit of Owl's Head
why: Climb of Owl's Head on Cherry Mountain from Rte 115 in Jefferson.

name: Peaked Hill Pond
quote: ending at the scenic shore of the pond at 1.7 miles
why: Easy gravel-road walk to Peaked Hill Pond near Thornton.

name: Province Pond
quote: Just a 1.6 mile hike in from the parking area, Province Pond Shelter is located on the edge of Province Pond.
why: Short hike to Province Pond and its shelter.

name: Rattle River Trail
quote: A gradual 1.7 miles will bring hikers to the Rattle River Shelter
why: Appalachian Trail walk from US Route 2 to Rattle River Shelter.

name: Rattlesnake Mountain (Rattlesnake Mtn Trailhead)
quote: This short (1.3 miles) steep trail accesses excellent views of the Baker River Valley from a scenic loop of the summit of Rattlesnake mountain.
why: Short steep trail with a summit loop above the Baker River Valley near Rumney.

name: The Roost
quote: requires a .8 mile walk along the road to complete a 1.2 mile loop
why: Short summit loop with Wild River Valley views near Gilead.

name: Sawyer Pond Trail
quote: Sawyer Pond is reached at 4.5 miles
why: Hike from the Kancamagus Highway to Sawyer Pond and its shelter.

name: Shell Pond Trail
quote: This trail is 1.8 miles between the Stone House Rd. and the Deer Hill Road.
why: Easy trail past Shell Pond between two roads near Stow, Maine.

name: Smarts Brook Trail
quote: connecting after 5.1 miles to the Sandwich Mountain trail just below Jennings Peak
why: Valley trail from Rte 49 up to the Sandwich Mountain Trail.

name: Lambert Ridge Trail (Smarts Mountain)
quote: the Lambert Ridge Trail which ascends the scenic Lambert Ridge and then steeply climbs to the summit of Smarts Mountain in 3.9 miles
why: Appalachian Trail climb of Smarts Mountain from Lyme-Dorchester Road.

name: Stony Brook Trail
quote: Park at the Stony Brook Trailhead for a 3.6 mile hike up to the Carter-Moriah Trail
why: Climb toward Mt. Moriah's south ledges from Rte 16.

name: Sugarloaf Trail
quote: The double peaks of the Sugarloafs can be ascended via the Sugarloaf Trail in 1.2 miles.
why: Short climb of the Sugarloafs off Zealand Road.

name: Townline Brook Trail
quote: At only .2 miles, the Townline Brook Trail presents hikers with an alluring opportunity to see three cascading waterfalls
why: Very short walk to three cascades near Jefferson.

name: Wachipauka Pond
quote: hikers can travel south on the AT to scenic Wachipauka Pond, reached in 2.3 miles
why: Appalachian Trail walk to Wachipauka Pond near Glencliff.

name: Velvet Rocks Trail
quote: the Velvet Rocks Trail (Appalachain Trail) travels towards Hanover and the Velvet Rocks Shelter at 3.1 miles
why: Appalachian Trail section from Trescott Road toward Hanover.

name: Unknown Pond (Unknown Pond South Trailhead)
quote: It is 3.3 miles from the trailhead to the Unknown Pond Tent site and the serene waters of Unknown Pond.
why: Hike to Unknown Pond in the Kilkenny area from York Pond Road.

name: Mt. Webster (Webster Cliff Trailhead)
quote: followed by Mt. Webster (3,910 ft.) at 3.3 miles
why: Webster Cliff Trail along the cliffs above Crawford Notch to Mt. Webster.

name: Winniweta Falls
quote: is 0.9 miles in length and accesses a waterfall
why: Short trail after fording the Ellis River to Winniweta Falls near Jackson.

name: Zealand Trail
quote: Zealand Falls Hut via the Zealand Trail is 2.3 miles.
why: Easy trail past beaver ponds to Zealand Falls Hut.
